risks.message: Row locks (FOR UPDATE/SHARE) only hold inside one transaction; lock and subsequent writes must share the same connection/transaction.

recommendations.message: Keep joins, aggregates, CTEs and bulk DML as parameterized SQL.
Receive an open connection; do not commit inside the function.
Map RAISE EXCEPTION to typed exceptions and RAISE NOTICE to logging.

architectural_decisions.decision: The function receives an open AsyncConnection and never commits/rolls back the outer transaction.
architectural_decisions.rationale: The caller owns the transaction; FOR UPDATE locks and the dependent writes must share the same transaction.

architectural_decisions.decision: Protected statements run inside `async with conn.begin_nested():`; the error-log insert runs in the except handler after the savepoint rollback.
architectural_decisions.rationale: A PL/pgSQL BEGIN...EXCEPTION block is a savepoint; without it the transaction would be aborted and the audit insert would fail.

architectural_decisions.decision: Each RAISE EXCEPTION maps to a typed exception subclassing TransferenciaError; WHEN OTHERS re-raise is reproduced by re-raising after logging.
architectural_decisions.rationale: Typed exceptions preserve the original error semantics for callers.

architectural_decisions.decision: All polymorphic positions (jsonb_build_object values, arithmetic with :p_valor) use CAST(:name AS type).
architectural_decisions.rationale: asyncpg cannot infer types in polymorphic positions; CAST is used instead of :: so SQLAlchemy still recognises the binds.

warnings: The original WHEN OTHERS also catches the validation RAISEs inside the block; this translation preserves that: validation errors raised inside the savepoint also produce a TRANSFERENCIA_ERRO audit entry before re-raising.
SQLERRM is approximated with str(exc); messages match the original format strings but the exact PostgreSQL error text for unexpected DB errors may differ.
The error audit insert itself can still fail (e.g. connection lost); in the original it would also propagate — behaviour is equivalent.
p_valor is expected as decimal.Decimal; passing float would lose exactness — NUMERIC(18,2) semantics are preserved end to end with Decimal.
